## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment default, which the project's CLI flag policy requires for every new flag under `cli/`. That is the only finding, and the exclusion logic and its tests have no other defects in this review's scope.

## Changes
Adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect` now skips files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped path. The PR also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests, plus a text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` without passing `--exclude`, nothing is excluded, because the flag's default is a hard-coded `default=[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` (same text in `.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`): "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment, as the policy expects, will silently archive files they meant to exclude. — Fix: Derive the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple globs in `docs/flags.md`, and add a case alongside `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
